newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia pipeline attacks said cost $38 million.
newsitem.headline: Colombia pipeline attacks said cost $38 million.

text.p: Leftist guerrillas attacked Colombia's main oil pipeline, which stretches from the northeast to the Atlantic coast, 40 times between January and September, causing total losses of about $38 million, state oil company Ecopetrol said Monday.

More than 79,200 barrels of oil, worth an estimated 1.6 billion pesos (about US$1.6 million) were spilled in the incidents -- mostly dynamite attacks carried out by National Liberation Army, Colombia's second largest rebel group.

Repair and clean-up work cost an estimated 4.8 billion pesos and more than 4.3 billion pesos in lost royalties, Ecopetrol said. According to the report, the attacks led to a total production loss of 1.1 million barrels, valued at almost 38 billion pesos (about $38 million).

The pipeline, which pumps a daily average of 200,000 barrels of crude, runs from the Cano Limon field, operated by U.S. multinational Occidental Petroleum, to the Covenas oil terminal on the Atlantic coast.
In the same period, the country's second largest pipeline, the Colombia, suffered nine attacks with a loss of 20,283 barrels of crude.
Both pipelines were paralyzed for the first time on record two weeks ago when Colombia's main oil union, USO, staged a 24-hour wildcat strike.
